office_does: One of 49 Washington State Senators, serving a four-year term writing state law and budgets for the 47th District (Kent, Auburn and Covington area of South King County).
race_blurb: Incumbent Democrat Claudia Kauffman faces Republican Covington City Councilmember Kristina Soltys. Both talk about affordability and public safety; they split on income taxes, housing policy tools, and state versus local control.

candidates.summary: Incumbent State Senator since 2022, who also held the seat from 2007 to 2011; former Muckleshoot Tribe intergovernmental affairs liaison. Running on affordability, housing supply with renter protections, and the safety net.
highlights: Voted yes on ESSB 6346, the 2026 tax on household income over $1 million that I-645 would repeal [S5]
Platform says the bottom 20% pay 'SEVEN times more of their income in taxes than billionaires' and proposes cutting property and sales taxes [S4]
Wants more housing supply and protection for renters from 'predatory price gouging' [S1]
Voted yes on ESHB 1296 (2025), the parental-rights amendments I-1 would undo [S6]
Endorsed by Gov. Ferguson, the mayors of Auburn, Covington and Kent, the State Labor Council and Washington Conservation Action [S1][S3][S11]

taxes.basis: Voted for the 2026 millionaires' tax (ESSB 6346) and argues the tax code burdens the poor far more than billionaires, proposing lower sales and property taxes instead.

spending.basis: Emphasizes expanded childcare, a 'robust' safety net and capital investments, without a stated program to expand public spending broadly.

housing.basis: Pairs housing supply with renter protections against 'predatory price gouging' and middle-income housing.

parental-rights.basis: Single record item: voted yes on ESHB 1296, which amended the I-2081 parental-rights law; no campaign statement on the topic.

experience.basis: Two Senate stints (2007-2011, 2022-present), committee leadership, and a 2026 legislative record.

candidates.summary: Covington City Councilmember since 2019 and former diagnostic medical sonographer who immigrated from Ukraine as a child. Running against the income tax and recent tax increases, and for permitting reform and police funding.
highlights: Opposes a state income tax ('Washington voters have rejected an income tax ten times') and says Olympia has 'a spending problem' [S4]
Said in July of the income tax repeal effort that an income tax 'doesn't belong here' [S5]
Favors permitting reform and market incentives; says state government should empower local communities rather than impose mandates [S4]
On the council: funded an additional police officer and started a community resource officer program for residents in crisis [S1]
Has raised more than the incumbent: $208.9K in contributions [S6]

taxes.basis: Repeated opposition to an income tax and to recent B&O and gas tax increases; calls the state's problem one of spending, not revenue.

spending.basis: 'Spending problem' framing and demand for budget results, while also backing funding for police and transportation.

housing.basis: Relies on permitting reform and market incentives over state mandates; no tenant-protection or public-housing proposals.

local-control.basis: 'Local communities know their neighborhoods. State government should empower them'; opposes top-down mandates, stated for housing.

safety.basis: Prioritizes fully funded police and more officers, paired with treatment resources and a community resource officer program.

experience.basis: Seven years on a city council but new to the Legislature, running against a long-serving incumbent.
